summary: Design and build a privacy-preserving hate speech detection (HSD) system that operates agnostically to author identity. The model uses a Transformer backbone (e.g., BERT/RoBERTa) with differentially private training (DP-SGD/DP-Adam) and adversarial identity disentanglement to decouple hate-signal from author-specific stylistic fingerprints, maximizing the privacy-HSD trade-off. A research note with ablation studies, privacy attack simulations, and Pareto-front analysis will accompany the prototype.
assumptions: Transformer-based encoder (BERT/RoBERTa variant) will serve as the backbone, fine-tuned on standard HSD benchmarks (Jigsaw, HateXplain) with privacy-augmented variants.

Primary privacy mechanism is differential privacy via DP-SGD combined with adversarial representation learning for identity disentanglement, avoiding full federated or homomorphic encryption in the initial prototype.
Evaluation metrics span both utility (F1/AUC for hate detection) and privacy (membership inference AUC, attribute inference accuracy, re-identification risk) to quantify the trade-off.
The prototype targets a centralized training setting with provable privacy guarantees (ε, δ) rather than distributed deployment, keeping computational overhead manageable for reproducibility.
